messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'saracen-prod-01' reporting sustained GPU saturation (100%) and request queuing for tenant SaracenCorp. Impact: degraded response times and request queue growth. Pager: eng-oncall.

maria: I’m on it, seeing huge backlog on the pool side. Queues jumping since 14:02 UTC.

aj: confirming, telemetry shows 0 free GPUs, 1200 queued requests, avg latency > 6s and some timeouts. Likely a single tenant spike.

karen: SaracenCorp on dedicated pool right? Any SLA hit reported from their side? I messaged their AM.

ryan: Saracen support: they reported errors at 14:05, says job bursts after a nightly run. They're investigating but need throughput now.

maria: quick ask: can we burst this tenant to shared-burst capacity? What are the policy constraints?

ops-lead: We have a configured burst override but it requires approval for enterprise pools because of isolation rules. @aj you have authority to approve emergency burst, ping when ready.

aj: I can approve emergency burst for 30m. Risks: could impact noise isolation and billing. Tradeoff: restore customer service. I approve. :white_check_mark:

maria: executing: devops-bot, apply burst to saracen-prod-01 -> shared-burst-2 for 30m.
devops-bot: executing command: ```repoolctl burst --pool saracen-prod-01 --target shared-burst-2 --duration 30m --reason "enterprise emergency" --ticket 54321```
devops-bot: OK: burst applied, provisioning 2x more GPUs from shared-burst-2. Expected available in ~40s.

aj: while that comes up, put a per-tenant rate limiter to prevent another huge push from causing the same. maria can you add a soft limit at 500 rps?

maria: doing config change: ```redwoodctl set-rate-limit --tenant SaracenCorp --rps 500 --soft=true --expire 30m```
maria: rate limiter in place.

oncall-2nd: seeing new GPUs come online, backlog draining. Latency down to ~1.2s and queue length falling.

ryan: Saracen says throughput looks normal again and they removed their internal batch job for now. Thanks.

ops-lead: Good. Now decisions: 1) keep burst for full 30m or end early once stable; 2) follow-ups: postmortem, permanent autoscale rule update, and customer communication.

aj: end burst only after sustained stable metrics for 10m. Also create a temporary migration plan if this repeats: move SaracenCorp to a new dedicated pool or increase their reserved capacity.

karen: I’ll draft a customer note (cc: legal/compliance if billing changes). Ryan, can you coordinate with Saracen AM to agree on next steps and share that we used burst?

maria: logging actions to ticket 54321: applied burst, set soft rate limit, monitored drain, requested postmortem.

aj: schedule an immediate follow-up call in 60m if any regressions. If stable at 30m, revert burst and remove soft rate limit gradually.

maria: revert plan executed at 14:45 UTC: devops-bot ran ```repoolctl revert --pool saracen-prod-01 --burst-id 54321``` and removed extra GPUs. Rate limit expiry left to run (30m). All metrics look steady.

devops-bot: Action log appended to ticket 54321, runbook steps executed: BURST_APPLY -> RATE_LIMIT -> MONITOR -> BURST_REVERT.

aj: Post-incident tasks: - owner: eng-ml to review Saracen workload pattern and suggest autoscale thresholds - owner: platform to add automated guardrail that triggers AM/ops when tenant surge reaches 70% of pool capacity - owner: sales/AM to discuss capacity commitment or migration.

ops-lead: assigning postmortem: tag eng-oncall, eng-runtime, customer-success. Please add timeline and root cause hypothesis. We’ll target infra postmortem doc in 72h.

ryan: I spoke to Saracen AM: they accept a brief outage explanation and want options (increase reserved GPUs or scheduled batch windows). Will sync with karen.

maria: closing this paging thread. If anything spikes back up I’ll re-open. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident closed for pager cycle. Ticket 54321 will remain open for postmortem and customer comms.
